facts.fact: AdImpact projects total political ad spending of $10.8 billion for the 2026 midterm cycle.
facts.quote: with AdImpact projecting $10.8 billion in total political ad spending

facts.fact: eMarketer projects CTV and OTT political ad spending to exceed $2.4 billion in a midterm cycle, up from roughly $1.5 billion in 2024.
facts.quote: projected to exceed $2.4 billion in a midterm cycle, up from roughly $1.5 billion in 2024

facts.fact: More than 60% of U.S. households have cut the cord or never had traditional pay TV, according to eMarketer's 2025 figure.
facts.quote: More than 60% of U.S. households have cut the cord or never had traditional pay TV.

facts.fact: eMarketer projects the share of U.S. households that have cut the cord or never had pay TV will climb past 63% by the end of 2026.
facts.quote: eMarketer projects this figure will climb past 63% by the end of 2026

facts.fact: Streaming accounts for 41% of all TV viewing time, according to Nielsen's Gauge report for Q4 2025.
facts.quote: Streaming now accounts for 41% of all TV viewing time.

facts.fact: Among adults 18 to 49, streaming's share of TV viewing is roughly 52%.
facts.quote: streaming's share is even higher at roughly 52%

facts.fact: According to Nielsen, adults 18 to 34 spend over 40% of their TV time on streaming platforms.
facts.quote: adults 18 to 34 spend over 40% of their TV time on streaming platforms

facts.fact: Nearly 60% of streaming viewers watch at least some ad-supported content, according to Hub Entertainment Research (2025).
facts.quote: Nearly 60% of streaming viewers watch at least some ad-supported content

facts.fact: FCC rules require broadcast stations to offer candidates the lowest unit rate during the 45 days before a primary and the 60 days before a general election.
facts.value: 45 days before a primary; 60 days before a general election
facts.quote: during the 45 days before a primary and 60 days before a general election

facts.fact: According to Nielsen (2025), adults 65+ watch an average of 6+ hours of traditional TV per day, compared with just over one hour of streaming.
facts.unit: hours per day of traditional TV
facts.quote: adults 65+ watch an average of 6+ hours of traditional TV per day, compared to just over one hour of streaming

facts.fact: Adwave, a vendor, says it starts CTV campaigns at $30 a day.
facts.quote: starting at just $30 a day

facts.fact: Traditional broadcast TV requires minimum buys of $5,000 to $50,000 or more, plus agency fees and weeks of lead time, according to the vendor.
facts.quote: Traditional broadcast TV requires minimum buys of $5,000 to $50,000 or more, plus agency fees and weeks of lead time.

facts.fact: The vendor states that CTV has no minimums on self-serve platforms.
facts.quote: CTV has no minimums on self-serve platforms.

facts.fact: The vendor says a candidate can run TV ads with a few hundred dollars using CTV.
facts.quote: A school board candidate, a state legislature challenger, or a ballot initiative committee can run TV ads with a few hundred dollars

facts.fact: The vendor lists OTT/CTV CPMs for political campaigns at $15-$35.
facts.quote: No minimums; CPMs of $15-$35; market-rate pricing

facts.fact: The vendor says Adwave lets campaigns launch CTV advertising for as little as $50.
facts.quote: Platforms like Adwave let you launch for as little as $50, making TV advertising accessible for even the smallest campaigns.

facts.fact: The vendor states that 60%+ of cord-cut households are reachable only via streaming.
facts.quote: Growing rapidly; 60%+ cord-cut households reachable only via streaming

facts.fact: The vendor lists linear TV completion rates as high at 95%+ because ads are non-skippable.
facts.quote: High (95%+; non-skippable)

facts.fact: The vendor lists CTV completion rates as high at 95%+, non-skippable on most platforms.
facts.quote: High (95%+; non-skippable on most platforms)

facts.fact: The vendor says linear TV is best for voter segments 55+ and CTV for 18-54 in its comparison table.
facts.quote: Best voter segments | 55+; live event watchers; broad statewide audiences | 18-54; cord-cutters; district-level and persuadable voter segments

facts.fact: The vendor states that linear TV placement and trafficking takes days to weeks, while OTT/CTV can launch in hours.
facts.quote: Speed to air | Days to weeks for placement and trafficking | Hours; some platforms launch same-day

facts.fact: The vendor describes linear TV as subject to FCC lowest unit rate protection for candidates, while CTV has none.
facts.quote: FCC lowest unit rate for candidates

facts.fact: For a congressional campaign with a $500K to $2M media budget, the vendor suggests 50-60% of TV budget to CTV/OTT.
facts.quote: CTV/OTT: 50-60% of TV budget.

facts.fact: For a congressional campaign, the vendor suggests 25-35% of TV budget to linear TV.
facts.quote: Linear TV: 25-35%.

facts.fact: For a congressional campaign, the vendor suggests 10-20% of budget to digital video.
facts.quote: Digital video (YouTube, social): 10-20%.

facts.fact: The vendor gives a congressional media budget range of $500K to $2M.
facts.quote: Congressional campaigns ($500K to $2M media budget)

facts.fact: The vendor gives a statewide media budget range of $2M to $10M+ and suggests 40-50% linear TV and 35-45% CTV/OTT.
facts.quote: Statewide campaigns ($2M to $10M+ media budget)

facts.fact: For a local campaign with a $10K to $100K media budget, the vendor suggests 65-80% of budget to CTV/OTT.
facts.quote: CTV/OTT: 65-80%.

facts.fact: For local races, the vendor suggests 0-15% of budget to linear TV, citing minimum buy requirements.
facts.quote: Linear TV: 0-15%.

facts.fact: For ballot measure campaigns, the vendor suggests 35-45% of budget to linear TV.
facts.quote: Linear TV: 35-45%.

facts.fact: For ballot measure campaigns, the vendor suggests 40-50% of budget to CTV/OTT.
facts.quote: CTV/OTT: 40-50%.

facts.fact: The vendor advises establishing campaign baseline metrics at least two weeks before the first ad airs.
facts.quote: Take these readings at least two weeks before your first ad airs.

facts.fact: The vendor describes linear TV measurement as panel-based (Nielsen) with DMA-level estimates.
facts.quote: Panel-based (Nielsen); DMA-level estimates

facts.fact: The Video Advertising Bureau (VAB), a third-party source cited by the page, found that multi-screen ad exposure increases unaided brand recall by 35% compared to single-screen exposure (VAB, 2024).
facts.quote: The VAB (Video Advertising Bureau) found that multi-screen ad exposure increases unaided brand recall by 35% compared to single-screen exposure

facts.fact: Adwave, the vendor, claims it can generate and launch a TV ad in under 10 minutes (vendor claim, not third-party verified).
facts.quote: Adwave's ability to generate and launch a TV ad in under 10 minutes makes same-day response possible for campaigns of any size.

facts.fact: Broadcast inventory tightens dramatically in September and October of election years.
facts.quote: Broadcast inventory tightens dramatically in September and October of election years.

facts.fact: There is no hard minimum budget on most self-serve CTV platforms, according to the page.
facts.quote: There's no hard minimum on most self-serve CTV platforms.

facts.fact: The page states that a campaign can start CTV testing with a few hundred dollars.
facts.quote: You can start testing with a few hundred dollars to see how targeting and creative perform before committing larger budgets.

facts.fact: Per the vendor's illustration, $500 to $1,000 in CTV spend can deliver 20,000 to 40,000 targeted impressions in a specific district.
facts.quote: even $500 to $1,000 in CTV spend can deliver 20,000 to 40,000 targeted impressions in a specific district

facts.fact: The page's rule of thumb is that if a campaign's district covers less than 30% of the DMA's population, its linear TV buy is probably more than 70% waste.
facts.quote: If your district covers less than 30% of the DMA's population, your linear buy is probably more than 70% waste.

facts.fact: CTV advertising does not fall under the same FCC regulations as broadcast TV, so campaigns do not receive lowest unit rate protections on CTV.
facts.quote: CTV advertising doesn't fall under the same FCC regulations as broadcast TV. That means you don't get lowest unit rate protections

facts.fact: Standard "paid for by" disclaimers are still required on CTV political ads, and FEC disclosure guidelines should be followed.
facts.quote: You still need standard "paid for by" disclaimers, and you should follow FEC guidelines on disclosure.
